changes.title: Show how to list CLI options with npx
changes.body:
## Summary

The npm README describes the CLI but gives readers no command to try. The introduction now includes this example.

```sh
npx ouch4ts --help
```

## Evidence

Ran the command in an empty directory with a fresh npm cache. It fetched `ouch4ts@0.1.0`, printed the CLI options, and exited with status 0.

## Merge danger

The change is one sentence in the README. Merging with `release:patch` triggers the first automated npm preview.
changes.head: jwood/readme-cli-help
changes.author: dumptruckman

changes.title: Preserve release tags and wait for npm verification
changes.body:
## Summary

The first npm preview needed manual recovery twice. GitHub renamed the draft that held the tarball, and the release job timed out while npm was making the version available.

```text
Update GitHub draft → send its original tag name with the progress update
npm accepts package → wait up to 20 minutes for the matching tarball and provenance
```

A retry that finds matching package metadata verifies the existing publication. Conflicting bytes or provenance stop the run immediately.

## Evidence

The release-command tests reproduce GitHub assigning an `untagged-*` name, an npm scan that exceeds the old 15-second window, recovery before provenance is available, and a connection that drops mid-download. The tests also check the deadline and rejection of a substituted source or tarball.

## Merge danger

Merging this `release:patch` PR triggers a public npm preview and refreshes [Release ouch4ts](https://github.com/dumptruckman/ouch4ts/pull/19). Merging that separate PR publishes stable `0.1.1`.

Fixes #17 (Preserve draft release tag names when recording progress).
Fixes #18 (Allow time for npm to expose a published version).
changes.head: jwood/fix-release-recovery
changes.author: dumptruckman
